findings.explanation: ir_045 represents internal argument transfer using a call opcode and call-role action, although this operation vocabulary defines call as delivery plus external acquisition. The source supplies four existing arguments to the represented callee; it does not independently acquire those formal values. The reported role barrier prevents processing from expressing this known transfer.
findings.suggestion: Classify this site as local argument transfer with outputs 0–3 mapped to inputs 1–4. Preserve its callable operand, the represented callee body, and the separate HTTP interaction at ir_049.

findings.explanation: ir_063 combines caught-object binding, string conversion, formatting and delivery behind one completion boundary. Its conditional intermediate-output availability cannot be realized with the supplied processing ports and scoping rules. String conversion can fail before exception_text exists, and formatting can fail before error_message exists; these outcomes must precede the print boundary.
findings.suggestion: Split the existing actions into local binding, protected string conversion, protected formatting and protected standard-output delivery. Place each intermediate output at its actual producer, merge actual escaping exceptions, and retain status-1 termination only after normal printing.

findings.explanation: The source establishes individually representable binding, conversion, formatting and print operations. Their conditional output availability requires separate CFG producer and completion boundaries rather than retaining the combined instruction's port limitation. Affected scope: ir_063 in the matching Exception handler, including intermediate outputs, escaping exceptions and standard-output delivery before ir_065.
findings.suggestion: Bind the caught object locally; stringify that object; prefix the resulting text with Error: ; deliver the completed message to standard output. Give conversion, formatting and printing their own normal and exceptional continuations, with status-1 exit following only normal delivery.
